name: Balangao

catalog_quote: Word stress in Balangao is phonemic, occurring on the ultimate or penultimate syllable of a full grammatical word, with or without affixes. All full words (see Sec. 1.1) must have stress. 'hawang 'doorway', ha'wang 'reach inside with hands', 'qale 'come', qa'le 'word'. A secondary stress occurs on every second syllable counting back from the main stress: pa"gingi'nahal 'sandy place', "bale'ngawngaw 'circle', qo"menpa"bale'ngawngaw 'cause it to be circled'. Clitics also have stress and they are the only full grammatical words that may occur as a single syllable with a single mora of length. ... Clitics do not set up secondary stress. ... Stress is characterized by 1) an added mora of vowel length when it occurs on non-final CV syllables, 2) a slight rise in pitch, and 3) intensity ...
sweep_summary: Balangao (bala1310) is in the catalog as 'lexical' on Shetler 1976 (Notes on Balangao Grammar, Sec. 1.5 p. 31: stress phonemic, ultimate or penultimate). The sweep found one stress-titled item, Shetler & Fetzer 1964 'The Obscuring of Word Accent in Balangao' (Oceanic Linguistics 3(1):101-109, DOI 10.2307/3622942), already in our bibliography; it is plainly about word accent in this language (Glottolog subject 'Suprasegmentals'; Shetler 1966 n. 4 names it as the detailed treatment). No open copy exists: Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall report it closed, JSTOR is paywalled behind a JS challenge, the archive.org microfilm scan of OL 3(1) is lending-restricted (text and search-inside blocked), HathiTrust has OL search-only and lacks vol. 3, Google Books and SIL entry 12319 return nothing. It is marked not-read, priority medium (same author as the 1976 grammar, so expected to corroborate, not change, the coding). The only first-hand statement read this sweep is Shetler 1966 'Balangao Phonemes' (PL A-8, open,: 'Word accent is also a phonemic feature of the dialect' (p. 2) and 'Accent is contrastive on the word level' (p. 7), with all accented examples on the final two syllables; it confirms but does not supersede the catalog source.

new_statements.quote: p. 2: "Word accent is also a phonemic feature of the dialect." p. 7, Sec. 3.4: "Accent is contrastive on the word level in the Balangao phonemic system. It is described in detail in the paper, \"The Obscuring of Word Accent in Balangao\"." (n. 4: Shetler, Jo and Hopkins, Anne Fetzer, Oceanic Linguistics 3:101-9, 1964). Accented examples on p. 2: dit'qal 'floor', du'mang 'other side', 'yato 'this', la'weng 'bad', hay'duq 'fish net', 'tongaw 'to stay home'.

new_statements.reading: First-hand SIL fieldworker statement (same author as the catalog's deciding source) that word accent is phonemic/contrastive in Balangao; it gives no explicit placement rule, but every accented example in the sketch carries the accent on the ultimate or penultimate syllable, consistent with the catalog's 'lexical, final-two-syllable window' coding. It defers the detailed account to Shetler & Fetzer 1964 (unobtained, paywalled).

audit.reasoning: (1) Deciding quotation confirmed verbatim in the held full PDF of Shetler 1976 at Sec. 1.5 p. 31 (PDF p. 33), with the p. 32 correlates passage and the Sec. 1.61 p. 35 stress-shift passage also matching the record's locators. (2) The source is the language's most extensive description (Glottolog MED, 254 pp.) with a dedicated multi-page stress section including minimal pairs ('hawang vs ha'wang, 'qale vs qa'le); coding 'lexical' with a right-edge two-syllable window and suffix-driven shift follows directly from it. the one unheld stress-specific work is Shetler & Fetzer 1964 (JSTOR DOI 10.2307/3622942, paywalled).
